score_method: Minimum mandatory visual-area score, not an average; every mandatory static visual check must pass strictly above 9.0.
pending_separate_evidence: Full GitHub byte/blob readback and independent archive gate
preservation: All previous source identities, original accepted images, rejected iterations and exact prompts remain preserved.

areas.finding: The ordinary Atlas boar is preserved as a compact charcoal/dark-brown bristled animal, pale broad muzzle and small ivory side tusks. It remains distinct from the older oversized reddish Tusk Boar appearance.
All four cardinal views and two obliques are distinct, correctly labeled, full-body and uncropped.
Four robust legs and paired cloven hoof forms are exposed across profiles and both obliques, with consistent front/rear joint direction and grounded feet.
A pair of small pale upward-curved tusks, broad two-nostril snout, paired ears and matching facial markings remain consistent; side views appropriately occlude the far tusk.
One short hanging tail attaches at the rump in both profiles, rear and rear oblique. It is separate from the bristle ridge and does not duplicate or detach.
Rounded compact torso, bristled back ridge, dark lower legs and brown/charcoal fur grouping remain coherent across the rotations.
Clean studio ground, grouped sculpted fur, clear face and readable panels satisfy static Havenline reference presentation.

source_interpretation_limit: The original Atlas supplies a small single-pose source appearance. Hidden reverse anatomy, fur grouping and fine texture placement are authored concept interpretation. Static sheets do not establish a native mesh, rig, animation or gameplay implementation.
minor_polish_limit: Individual fur-tuft outlines and thin tail profile vary slightly between independently illustrated angles without a required identity, attachment or count contradiction.
